findings.description: The dashboard does not cap at 3 items, and the overflow label it renders is factually false to the user. The spec is 'The dashboard shows at most 3 items (DASHBOARD_GUIDANCE_CAP = 3); when more than 3 REQUIRED items exist, the overflow must be surfaced as a count.' capGuidanceItems instead places EVERY REQUIRED item into `visible` with no truncation, and additionally reports requiredOverflowCount = required.length - 3. GuidanceWorkQueue then renders every element of `visible` AND renders the string '(+N more required)' beside the heading. So with 5 REQUIRED items the user sees all 5 cards and is simultaneously told that 2 more required items exist beyond what is shown -- when those 2 are already on screen. Even granting the implementation's own reading ('preserve REQUIRED visibility' beats the numeric cap), the rendered label is wrong under either reading: a count of hidden items is displayed when nothing is hidden. On a compliance work-queue whose entire premise is an accurate 'these are the things needing your attention', an overflow indicator that miscounts is a user-facing correctness defect, not a cosmetic one.
findings.evidence: cap.ts:39-48 returns { visible: required, requiredOverflowCount: max(0, required.length - 3) } whenever required.length >= 3 -- `required` is the full unsliced array. guidance-work-queue.tsx:86-90 renders '(+{requiredOverflowCount} more required)'; :94 maps over the whole of result.visible. My own probe P6 (5 REQUIRED I19 items through the real runGuidancePipeline) printed: 'P6 visible.length = 5 | requiredOverflowCount = 2 | ids = I19:ship-a,I19:ship-b,I19:ship-c,I19:ship-d,I19:ship-e'. The shipped cap.test.ts:106-115 asserts visible == ['r1','r2','r3','r4'] with requiredOverflowCount == 1, codifying the behaviour as intended.

findings.description: I22's impact forcing is gated on an extra condition the specification does not contain, so shipments that must be de-escalated to APPROVAL keep FILING. The spec is unconditional on the declaration's own state: 'if a shipment is a non-member of a Declaration that covers its reporting period (i.e., the shipment's id is NOT in that declaration's member_shipment_ids) -- that shipment's I19 item KEEPS its REQUIRED priority, but its impact is forced from FILING to APPROVAL.' The implementation's isNonMemberOfBlockedDeclaration additionally requires hasI22Condition(declaration), i.e. declaration.status === 'DRAFT' AND completeness_report !== null AND !completeness_report.complete. Two concrete, reachable shapes therefore diverge: (a) a DRAFT declaration whose completeness report has never been generated (completeness_report null), and (b) any non-DRAFT declaration (READY / FILED_RECORDED). In both, a non-member shipment is told its impact is FILING. That is the exact false reassurance I22 exists to prevent: the user is told that marking this shipment ready keeps it eligible for a filing that, per the declaration's own persisted member snapshot, it is not part of. The reason string shown to the user reinforces the error verbatim ('A declaration exists for this reporting period -- marking this shipment ready keeps it eligible to be included when that declaration is filed.'). No v2.1.1 specification document exists anywhere in the repository to corroborate the implementation's 'D DRAFT with blockers' reading -- grep -ril 'I22' matches only i19.ts and its own test -- so the extra gate is unsourced.
findings.evidence: i19.ts:60-68 (hasI22Condition) and :82-93 (isNonMemberOfBlockedDeclaration, which requires hasI22Condition before considering non-membership). My own probe: 'P1 impact = FILING priority = REQUIRED' for a DRAFT declaration with completeness_report null and the shipment absent from member_shipment_ids; 'P2 impact = FILING' for a FILED declaration with blockers and the shipment a non-member. Spec requires APPROVAL in both. The shipped i19.test.ts:243-271 and :273-301 assert FILING for exactly these shapes, codifying the divergence as intended. (Probe P3 confirms the multi-declaration case is handled correctly once the gate does pass.)

findings.description: Above roughly 220 draft shipments, the guidance dashboard tells the user, affirmatively, that nothing needs their attention -- while every one of those shipments needs action. listDraftShipmentsWithLines issues a single PostgREST request whose filter embeds every draft shipment id: .in('shipment_id', rows.map(r => r.id)). That URL crosses the gateway's URI limit at n=220 and the request fails with HTTP 414. The function's error branch is `if (linesError) { return []; }`, so the failure is swallowed: deriveI19Items receives an empty shipment list, the pipeline produces nothing, and GuidanceWorkQueue renders its empty state, the literal sentence 'Nothing needs your attention right now.' There is no error state, no partial result, and no signal to the user or to logs that a query failed. Below that threshold the same code path is degraded differently but still silently: PostgREST's max_rows = 1000 truncates the shipment_lines select without an error, so once the org's draft shipments carry more than 1000 lines in aggregate (e.g. ~334 shipments at 3 lines each), the shipments whose lines fall past row 1000 receive an empty lines array, transitionShipment then rejects them with NO_LINES, and their REQUIRED guidance item silently disappears. Neither query is ordered or paginated, so which shipments are dropped is arbitrary. A compliance product issuing a false all-clear is materially worse than showing nothing at all.
findings.evidence: list-draft-shipments-with-lines.ts:58-72 (unbounded .in filter; `if (linesError) return []`), :38-53 (unbounded shipments select, also `return []` on error). guidance-work-queue.tsx:71-77 renders 'Nothing needs your attention right now.' for an empty visible list. Live bisection against the running stack, using the identical request shape: LAST OK n=219 urlLen=8175 status=200; FIRST FAIL n=220 urlLen=8212 status=414 'URI too long' (also confirmed 414 at n=500/1000/2000). max_rows=1000 in supabase/config.toml:18, confirmed live: default_emission_values holds 12,540 rows by direct SQL but an unbounded PostgREST select returned exactly 1000 with no error. i19.test.ts:135-146 confirms that a shipment with an empty lines array emits no item.

findings.area: domain/guidance/aggregate.ts + types.ts (aggregate identity vs. its documented contract)
findings.description: An aggregate's id is not membership-sensitive, directly contradicting the contract types.ts states for it, with the consequence that contract was written to prevent. types.ts documents that a GuidanceItem id 'must change if the underlying condition materially changes (e.g. an aggregate's id changes when its membership changes, so a stale dismissal naturally stops matching rather than silently continuing to suppress a now-different set of items).' aggregate.ts computes the id purely from (rule, parent.type, parent.id) -- membership is not an input, so the id is identical whether the group has 4 members or 40. A dismissal recorded against a 4-member aggregate therefore keeps suppressing the same group after it grows, which is precisely 'silently continuing to suppress a now-different set of items'. Not blocking today because it is unreachable: I19 is the only implemented rule, it emits parent: null so it never aggregates, and it is always REQUIRED so dismissal never applies to it. It will become reachable with the first non-REQUIRED aggregating rule.
findings.evidence: types.ts:56-62 (the documented contract) vs aggregate.ts:78-80 (`const id = `aggregate:${best.rule}:${best.parent?.type}:${best.parent?.id}``). My probe P7 printed: 'P7 aggregate id @4 = aggregate:LINE:shipment:S1 | @5 = aggregate:LINE:shipment:S1 | same = true', then 'P7 after dismissing the 4-member aggregate, the 5-member aggregate visible? = false'.

findings.area: app/guidance-actions.ts (dismissal write path) + app/feedback/actions.ts (its justifying comment)
findings.description: The dismissal Server Action accepts an arbitrary, unbounded item_key from the client, and the comment used to justify exempting it from rate limiting is factually false. app/guidance-actions.ts asserts that dismissal is 'a low-risk, idempotent, per-user write bounded by the number of real guidance items that exist for this org (never unboundedly user-suppliable), so this is deliberately NOT rate-limited'; app/feedback/actions.ts repeats the claim ('unlike guidance dismissal, which is capped by the number of real guidance items that exist') to justify rate-limiting feedback but not dismissal. In fact the action reads formData.get('itemKey') and forwards it after only a `typeof === 'string' && length > 0` check -- there is no validation that the key corresponds to any derivable guidance item, and no length bound (item_key is `text`; the only CHECK is length > 0). The unique constraint is per (org_id, user_id, item_key), so distinct fabricated keys never collide. Any authenticated member can therefore write unbounded rows of arbitrary size into their tenant's guidance_dismissals. No cross-tenant exposure and no data corruption -- hence YELLOW -- but it is real per-tenant storage abuse, and the false premise in the comment is what is keeping the rate limiter off.
findings.evidence: app/guidance-actions.ts:23-30 (the claim) and :34-62 (the unvalidated pass-through); app/feedback/actions.ts:36-43 (the repeated claim). Live psql probe inside a real `begin; ... rollback;`, acting as an ordinary authenticated MEMBER via `set local role authenticated` + request.jwt.claims: 'ROWS_WRITTEN_BY_ORDINARY_MEMBER|502|200000' (502 rows, longest item_key 200,000 bytes). Rollback verified real: BEFORE_TOTAL_ROWS=0, AFTER_TOTAL_ROWS=0, AFTER_PROBE_ORG_ROWS=0, probe org and user both gone. Nothing was committed.

findings.description: The 'no audit-event dependency' architecture test detects module imports only, not a direct read of the audit_events table. Its import check is real and does go red on a genuine import (I verified this, then reverted). But a guidance file can read the audit trail with no import at all -- supabase.from('audit_events').select(...) -- and the test stays green, so the hard rule is enforced against the likely accident but not against the mechanism itself. Adding an /audit_events|audit_event/ table-name pattern alongside the import pattern would close it. The companion 'no reason column' check is genuinely effective (verified red on an injected dismissal_reason column) and its author already found and fixed the \b-vs-substring bug that would have weakened it.

findings.area: application/guidance + application/shipments (error posture of the guidance read path)
findings.description: Every read feeding the guidance dashboard fails silently into a value indistinguishable from 'all clear'. listDraftShipmentsWithLines returns [] on either query error, listDeclarations returns [] on error, and listGuidanceDismissals returns an empty Set on error. Each is individually defensible and the dismissals one is explicitly modelled on existing precedent, but composed they mean any transient failure of any of the three renders the affirmative sentence 'Nothing needs your attention right now.' rather than a degraded or unknown state. This is the mechanism that makes B3 invisible, and it would equally mask an outage. A compliance work-queue would be safer with an explicit 'couldn't load your guidance' state distinct from a genuine empty queue. Recorded separately from B3 because it is a design posture worth revisiting even once B3's specific query shape is fixed.
findings.evidence: list-draft-shipments-with-lines.ts:47-53 and :70-72; list-declarations.ts:41-44; list-guidance-dismissals.ts:37-39 (with its own doc comment explaining the fail-closed-to-empty choice); guidance-work-queue.tsx:71-77 renders the all-clear for an empty visible list.

findings.description: Documentation-only mismatch. The migration comment on the unique constraint says 'the application's own upsert (onConflict) relies on this constraint rather than a SELECT-then-INSERT race', but dismissGuidanceItem does not upsert -- it performs a plain .insert() and treats SQLSTATE 23505 as success. The end behaviour is equivalent and correct; the comment describes an implementation that does not exist, which will mislead the next reader.

summary: FAIL: three BLOCKING findings, five YELLOW. The slice is, in most respects, careful and genuinely well-tested work -- the pipeline order matches the spec exactly, I19 correctly reuses the real transitionShipment rather than re-implementing eligibility, member_shipment_ids is read as a persisted snapshot with exact matching, the aggregation 3-vs-4 boundary test is real and exercises both sides with AGGREGATE_THRESHOLD === 4, dismissal-ignored-when-REQUIRED is correct, the protected regulatory zone is untouched, exactly the two intended tables were added, scope discipline is clean, and RLS isolation for both new tables genuinely ran against local Supabase (24 tests, not skipped) covering cross-org and cross-user-within-org in both directions. pnpm typecheck and the full pnpm test suite both pass (1938 passed / 6 skipped). The two mandated architecture probes confirmed the reason-column check and the audit-import check both genuinely go red on a real violation. But three defects block shipping. B2: I22's impact forcing is gated on an unsourced extra condition ('D DRAFT with blockers') that the verbatim specification does not contain, so a shipment that is a non-member of a declaration covering its period is told its impact is FILING -- the precise false reassurance I22 exists to prevent -- whenever that declaration is non-DRAFT or has no generated completeness report; my own probes P1 and P2 demonstrate both shapes returning FILING where the spec requires APPROVAL, and the shipped tests codify the divergence as intended. B1: the dashboard does not cap at 3 -- capGuidanceItems returns every REQUIRED item unsliced and the UI renders all of them while simultaneously displaying '(+N more required)', so with 5 required items the user sees 5 cards and is told 2 more are hidden; the label is false under any reading of the cap semantics. B3: the guidance fetch embeds every draft shipment id in one PostgREST .in() filter, which I bisected live to fail with HTTP 414 from 220 shipments upward (last OK n=219 at 8175 bytes, first failure n=220 at 8212), and the error branch returns [] -- so an importer with a few hundred pending draft shipments is shown the affirmative sentence 'Nothing needs your attention right now.'; below that threshold the confirmed max_rows=1000 silent truncation drops arbitrary shipments' lines and makes their REQUIRED items vanish just as quietly. On a CBAM compliance tool a false all-clear is worse than no answer. The YELLOWs are a genuine-but-currently-unreachable aggregate-identity bug that contradicts its own documented contract (probe P7: identical id at 4 and 5 members, and a dismissed aggregate stays suppressed after growth), an unvalidated and unbounded item_key write path whose no-rate-limit justification comment is demonstrably false (502 fabricated rows including one of 200,000 bytes, written as an ordinary member and rolled back for real), an audit-dependency test that catches imports but not a direct audit_events table read, the fail-silently-to-all-clear posture of the whole guidance read path, and one inaccurate migration comment. All probes were reverted and the working tree was confirmed clean at every step; the only mutation-oriented database probe ran inside a real psql begin/rollback with before-and-after row counts verified at zero.
